Method 1 — sum $P(10),P(11),P(12)$
$P(X\ge10)=\binom{12}{10}(0.72)^{10}(0.28)^2+\binom{12}{11}(0.72)^{11}(0.28)+\binom{12}{12}(0.72)^{12}$. [M1]
Guidance: Use at least one valid binomial term $\binom{12}{x}p^x(1-p)^{12-x}$ with $0<x<12$ and $0<p<1$.
$=0.193725+0.0905726+0.0194084$. [A1]
Guidance: Include all required direct-tail terms, with none omitted, in an expression leading to the answer.
$=0.304$. [B1]
Guidance: Award a result greater than $0.3036$ and at most $0.304$.
Method 2 — complement
$P(X\ge10)=1-\sum_{x=0}^{9}\binom{12}{x}(0.72)^x(0.28)^{12-x}$. [M1]
Guidance: Use at least one valid binomial term $\binom{12}{x}p^x(1-p)^{12-x}$ with $0<x<12$ and $0<p<1$.
$=1-[\binom{12}{0}(0.28)^{12}+\binom{12}{1}(0.72)(0.28)^{11}+\cdots+\binom{12}{9}(0.72)^9(0.28)^3]$. [A1]
Guidance: The complement expression must include every term from $x=0$ through $x=9$, with none omitted, and lead to the answer.
$=0.304$. [B1]
Guidance: Award a result greater than $0.3036$ and at most $0.304$.
Total: 3

$P(X<40)\approx P\!\left(Z<\frac{39.5-46.8}{\sqrt{22.464}}\right)$ [M1]
Guidance: Substitute the candidate’s mean and variance into a standardisation formula. Do not use variance as the denominator, square the standard deviation, or take an extra square root.
$\frac{39.5-46.8}{\sqrt{22.464}}=-1.540$ [M1]
Guidance: Use continuity correction $39.5$ or $40.5$ in the standardisation formula.
$P(Z<-1.540)=1-0.9382$ [M1]
Guidance: Use the appropriate cumulative normal area from the final standardisation process; the result must be a probability.
$P(X<40)=0.0618$ [A1]
Guidance: Award a result from $0.06175$ inclusive to $0.0618$ inclusive.
